event_description: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), and the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Health Sector Cybersecurity Coordination Center (HC3) release a joint alert regarding a rise in cyberattacks targeting healthcare organizations. The alert describes the tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) used by cyber criminals, including phishing emails, ransomware, remote hacking, distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks, and data exfiltration from healthcare organizations.
business_impact: No direct impact reported; increased awareness of threats targeting healthcare organizations

event_description: <Organization> employees receive e-mail notifications from your managed service provider (MSP) requesting they update their profiles prior to the launch of a new human resources (HR) system. The e-mail contains a link and attachment named Update_Form.docx. Employees working at remote workstations across facilities click the link and are asked to log into their web portal. Upon logging in, they are brought to a 404 Error Page. Some employees also open the attachment and click to allow macros to run.
business_impact: Potential credential theft and malware infection through suspicious emails and attachments

event_description: Manufacturer’s updates are pushed for installation on patient monitors. The updates are downloaded from the manufacturer’s website and installed without issue.
business_impact: No negative impact reported; patient monitor updates installed successfully

event_description: A third-party electronic medical record (EMR) vendor shows up unannounced at your facility to update equipment. The vendor needs to patch a recently discovered vulnerability in software used on several devices, including workstations, imaging and radiology equipment, bedside monitors, and other clinical devices.
business_impact: Potential compromise of clinical devices and systems if the vulnerability remains unpatched

event_description: Radiology reports an issue with their Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) machine accepting patient information, stating their computer is locking up or taking a long time to load. The reports also indicate an extraordinary amount of time is required to pull images for each patient. The delays have resulted in patient appointments running more than two hours behind schedule.
business_impact: MRI system delays causing patient appointments to run more than two hours behind schedule

event_description: A system administrator discovers active accounts for IT employees that left the organization over the past 12 months. The administrator closes them out.
business_impact: Potential misuse of former employees' active IT accounts; accounts were deactivated

event_description: Nurses on the floor report that patient records are displaying incorrect information about medication, diagnosis, and personal information.
business_impact: Incorrect patient records creating risks to patient safety and clinical decisions

event_description: Staff discover bedside monitor data is inaccurate and the infusion pumps are not operating properly and are failing to deliver infusions at the correct rate.
business_impact: Inaccurate monitoring data and incorrect infusion rates threatening patient safety

event_description: Ransomware messages appear on computers throughout <organization>, and users report they are unable to access their files. A message is displayed that reads: “Hello! Your files have been liberated. We have your data. But do not fear because for the sum of $1,000,000 your files will be returned. The decryption key will expire in 72 hours. Please submit payment to the wallet below or we will start selling patient data to the highest bidder.”
business_impact: Files unavailable, $1 million ransom demand, and threatened exposure of patient data

event_description: Current and former patients contact the hospital saying they received calls from someone claiming to have access to their medical records and offering to return them for a fee. The patients are provided enough information to verify the callers have their records. Patients say the fees range from a few hundred dollars to more than a thousand and are demanding to know why these individuals have their records. Some say they contacted law enforcement; others contacted the media. Many are threatening legal action.
business_impact: Patient information exposed; extortion attempts, complaints, and threatened legal action

event_description: Patients request transfers to other local hospitals because they feel unsafe. They also demand the return of all their medical records, as well as the removal of their records from your network. The patients state they will never return your facilities.
business_impact: Loss of patient trust, requests for hospital transfers, and potential loss of patients

event_description: CISA and the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) launch a joint response to a global cybersecurity incident in which malicious actors executed ransomware attacks against Managed Service Providers (MSPs) and their downstream customers. The malicious actors leveraged a vulnerability in a popular Remote Monitoring and Management (RMM) software. Once the malware was discovered, the software was shut down. Impacted MSPs were unable to provide services to customers worldwide, affecting the critical functions of entities across sectors, including gas stations, pharmacies, railways, and public broadcasting. Your organization is not impacted at this time.
business_impact: Global service disruptions affecting MSP customers; no direct impact on the organization

event_description: Your organization contracts a new MSP who is known as a trusted partner across your sector. Their platform is installed and updated with no alerts from your intrusion detection software.
business_impact: No negative impact reported during onboarding of a new managed service provider

event_description: Data from multiple sector partners is found on the DarkWeb. Some of these sector partners recommended your new MSP to you.
business_impact: Partner data exposed; possible concerns about the security of the new MSP

event_description: Your IT department authorizes the installation of a software update from your new MSP on one of your critical systems. The update will improve system functionality.
business_impact: No negative impact reported; authorized software update intended to improve functionality

event_description: Employees at your organization are unable to sign in to the network when they arrive in the morning. Your IT helpdesk is inundated with calls reporting the issue. Your IT department contacts your MSP, but they are unable to reach the MSP <helpdesk/customer service representative>.
business_impact: Employees unable to access the network; MSP support unavailable

event_description: Employees are still unable to access your network. There are significant impacts to business-critical systems.
business_impact: Continued network outage significantly affecting business-critical systems

event_description: An independent cybersecurity company discovers your MSP was the victim of a cyber incident that impacted their widely used platform. The cybersecurity company suspects your MSP’s customers unknowingly had malware on their system for up to two years. The company states any user of the MSP’s platform could be affected by the malicious code, and recommends organizations take steps to identify and eradicate it.
business_impact: MSP platform compromised; potential malware exposure affecting customers

event_description: The IT department starts an internal investigation. Their investigation discovers anomalous traffic in your network over the past seven months.
business_impact: Possible network compromise requiring investigation; full impact not yet established

event_description: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) issues an Alert regarding a new ransomware variant. This ransomware is being used in a campaign targeting state, local, tribal, and territorial governments, as well as private sector firms.
business_impact: No direct impact reported; warning about a new ransomware campaign

event_description: It has been one year since the developer of your current operating system announced that they will no longer develop security patches for your operating system. The final security patch was installed last week. This vulnerability was identified in your recently completed annual risk assessment.
business_impact: Increased security risk because the operating system no longer receives security patches

event_description: An employee informs their manager that their work laptop was stolen from their car overnight. The laptop contained sensitive organizational information.
business_impact: Potential exposure of sensitive organizational information stored on a stolen laptop

event_description: Members of your <Finance> department receive an email that appears to be from the Vice President of <Finance>. It instructs them to access a PDF containing details about an unpaid bill from a third-party vendor supporting your organization. Several employees call the Vice President to verify the email’s authenticity. She replies that she did not send it, and that there is no outstanding vendor bill. Nevertheless, some employees still open the PDF.
business_impact: Potential malware infection or unauthorized access after employees opened a suspicious PDF

event_description: An increase in Domain Name System (DNS) traffic outside of standard business hours is flagged by your organization’s intrusion detection system and an alert is sent to your <IT team/Security Operations Center>. Upon further investigation of the system logs, they discover that a significant amount of data was sent from known HR employee IP addresses to external IP addresses.
business_impact: Significant data transferred to external IP addresses; possible exposure of sensitive information

event_description: Computers throughout your organization display a blank red screen. A ransom message then appears demanding <insert ransom amount (e.g., $53,000.00)> worth of Bitcoin for the decryption key and a warning that the key will expire unless payment is received within 48 hours.
business_impact: Computers locked by ransomware, disrupting operations and triggering a ransom demand

event_description: A security researcher uncovers a series of posts from a well-known hacker group on the Dark Web and contacts your organization. The researcher believes that the posts are genuine, and the threat actors gained access to PII, including <employee social security numbers, bank account and routing number information, etc.>. The hacker group shared a limited number of data records to substantiate their claims and assert their intention to sell the data.
business_impact: Employee personal and financial information exposed; threatened sale of stolen data

event_description: News outlets report on the cyber incident. Several news outlets contact your organization for comments on the ransomware infection and data breach.
business_impact: Media attention following the ransomware incident and data breach; reputational risk

event_description: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) releases an alert with details on the Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) that are routinely and frequently exploited by malicious cyber actors. Your information technology (IT) department identifies a vulnerability in a type of microprocessor that is widely deployed within your organization, which may grant an attacker access to sensitive data.
business_impact: Potential unauthorized access to sensitive data through a microprocessor vulnerability

event_description: After investigating the vulnerability, your IT department determines that it is necessary to replace the impacted microprocessor. Due to the expense and time needed to replace the impacted microprocessors, it is determined that a year-long roll out and update strategy is required.
business_impact: Costly and time-consuming hardware replacement; security risk remains during rollout

event_description: At the end of a long workday, one of your employees inadvertently sends an email containing PII from <your organization, customers, clients, etc.> to several external contacts.
business_impact: Personally identifiable information accidentally disclosed to external contacts

event_description: The PII disclosure is discussed during the morning meeting. A representative from a key department loudly berates another team member about the PII breach. Their behavior is far outside your organization’s definition of acceptable conduct. This representative, though highly competent in their field, has engaged in similar behavior in the past and had been formally cautioned by Human Resources that any future instances of such conduct would result in termination.
business_impact: Workplace conflict following the PII disclosure; potential personnel consequences

event_description: Senior management makes the decision to terminate the employee due to their unprofessional conduct. They react poorly to the notification, screaming expletives at senior management and warning them that “You will be sorry!” for firing them.
business_impact: Risk of retaliation from a terminated employee; no cyberattack established at this stage

event_description: Staff begins the process of replacing impacted microprocessor chips. Due to high demand for replacement materials, the estimated process will take 18 months to complete.
business_impact: Extended security exposure and resource demands due to an 18-month replacement process

event_description: During a meeting with a key vendor, it is revealed that they have hired your recently terminated employee. The vendor assures your representatives that the employee will not attend  any meetings with your organization.
business_impact: Possible third-party access risk involving a former employee; no incident confirmed

event_description: Several employees contact the help desk with complaints of difficulties accessing information on shared network drives. Some files appear to have been renamed, moved, or deleted. The IT department can recover the missing files from backups, but any work completed  following the creation of the latest backup has been lost.
business_impact: Files moved or deleted; lost work since the last backup

event_description: The IT department reviews logs to determine the issue with the files. They quickly identify the presence of an unauthorized administrator-level account. The account is immediately deactivated.
business_impact: Unauthorized administrator account discovered and deactivated; potential system compromise

event_description: The IT department determines the unknown administrator account was added to the system by exploiting the microprocessor vulnerability. After accessing the memory of the machine, the attacker was able to obtain an administrator password used to install a recent security patch, create a new administrator account, and move laterally through the system.
business_impact: Administrator credentials compromised, enabling privileged access and lateral movement

event_description: The IT department determines that the Internet Protocol address used to create the unauthorized administrative account belongs to your third-party vendor.
business_impact: Unauthorized account creation traced to a vendor-associated IP address; responsibility unconfirmed

event_description: Staff is frantically calling your support desk. Files crucial to your organization’s ability to complete its core functions appear to have been deleted.
business_impact: Critical organizational files appear deleted, threatening core business operations

event_description: A senior finance employee receives what appears to be an email from another senior-level employee urgently requesting they review a shared document. The following month, employees begin reporting to <HR/Finance/Payroll> that their paychecks were not deposited into their bank accounts. <HR/Finance/Payroll> investigates and finds your payroll system is not working properly. The next day, all employees are locked out of their computers via ransomware. A ransom note is displayed on employee computers, threatening to sell <employee and/or customer personally Identifiable information (PII)> on the dark web if the ransom of <$XXX,XXX> is not paid. A small amount of <employee and/or customer> bank account information is posted on the dark web as proof of the threat.
business_impact: Payroll disruption, employee computer lockouts, ransom demand, and exposure of bank account information

event_description: Your IT department determines that a known exploited vulnerability on the network is not currently a priority for patching/mitigation. The next day, a disgruntled senior-level IT employee is terminated. Before departing, the employee angrily accuses your organization of wrongful termination. One month later, several employees contact the help desk reporting they cannot access information on network shared drives. IT investigates and discovers sensitive files <including intellectual property/protected files> appear to have been removed. Upon further investigation, an administrator account accessed file servers throughout the network and exfiltrated data to an external IP address. This account belonged to the terminated employee. A post goes viral on social media in which an anonymous hacker claims responsibility for the breach and theft of critical information, including sensitive employee information, from your organization and that of your <customers/constituents/partners/shareholders>. <Customers/constituents/partners/shareholders> are requesting information about the breach. Media outlets are also requesting comments and interviews.
business_impact: Sensitive information stolen, including intellectual property; external data exposure and reputational risk
